themes_detail.label: Indoor air quality crisis
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints surged to 6 THIS WEEK, a 500% spike versus the 8-week baseline of 1.0 weekly complaints (z-score: 5.77), suggesting a concentrated acute event or widespread building ventilation failure affecting multiple residents simultaneously.
evidence: 6 indoor air quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (500% increase)
Z-score of 5.77 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Concurrent spike in outdoor air quality complaints (4 last week vs. 0.6 avg, 540% increase) suggests environmental trigger
reporting_angles: Interview residents filing complaints to identify common location or building—determine if single source (construction, industrial facility, heating plant) or distributed problem
Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection to determine if air monitoring data corroborates resident reports and identify sources

themes_detail.label: Curb and street sign deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints hit 3 THIS WEEK, a 2300% spike from 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69), while street sign damage/missing complaints have surged 500-2300% over the past 2-3 weeks, suggesting infrastructure failure across the district.
evidence: Curb condition: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69)
Street sign missing: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69)
Street sign damaged: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (500% increase, z-score: 3.54)
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify if deterioration is concentrated in specific blocks or neighborhood-wide—visual survey to assess scope
Request Department of Transportation accident/pothole data and maintenance schedules for past 60 days to determine if recent weather or construction caused damage

themes_detail.label: Elevator failures accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints jumped to 24 complaints 2 weeks ago, a 220% increase from 7.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.62), indicating widespread building system failures affecting tenant access and safety in residential units.
evidence: 24 elevator complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 7.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (220% increase, z-score: 4.62)
Department of Buildings has received repeated budget requests to 'assign additional building inspectors' (ongoing unsolved issue per CB records)
187 alteration permits filed in past 90 days suggest active renovation work that may be impacting building infrastructure
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings had multiple elevator complaints and interview residents about length of outages, age of units, and landlord response time
Obtain DOB inspection records for these buildings to determine if violations were cited and whether landlords have been issued compliance deadlines

themes_detail.label: Building code violations surge
themes_detail.summary: Building/use violations spiked to 6 complaints 2 weeks ago, a 700% increase from 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 7.94), potentially indicating illegal conversions, overcrowding, or unauthorized commercial use in residential structures.
evidence: 6 building/use violations 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (700% increase, z-score: 7.94)
21 new building permits filed in past 90 days suggesting active construction; 893-895 East 167th Street rezoning is in ZM review stage
Community board has standing request for 'assign additional building inspectors,' indicating chronic enforcement gaps
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaint addresses with DOB inspection database to identify specific buildings and violation types (illegal conversion, occupancy overages, commercial-in-residential)
Interview DOB about enforcement capacity and timeline for addressing complaints in this district given budget constraints

themes_detail.label: Sewage system strain
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints reached 11 three weeks ago, a 283% increase from 2.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.43), alongside 197 water leak complaints over 90 days, suggesting aging infrastructure or blockages affecting multiple properties.
evidence: 11 sewer complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.9 weekly average (283% increase, z-score: 4.43)
197 water leak complaints over 90-day period (2.2 weekly rate) indicates sustained infrastructure stress
Community board has standing request for 'Other capital budget request for DEP,' suggesting water/sewer infrastructure is chronic concern
reporting_angles: Request DEP records of main breaks, combined sewer overflow events, and infrastructure age in this district over past 6 months
Identify cluster of sewer and water leak complaints by location to determine if isolated infrastructure issue or neighborhood-wide aging system problem
